claims.assertion: The ride was a RydeTAXI metered trip (F6 shows base + distance + time units totalling $24.80), so extra kilometres driven flow straight into the fare and any unexcused deviation is refundable per RD-2's metered branch.

The GPS record shows the trip covered 10.7 km against an optimal 8.4 km, i.e. +2.3 km (+27%) more than the shortest and most direct route (F1), which the driver was obliged to take absent reasonable cause.

The excess is concentrated in a single off-route segment 12:12–12:16, where 2.93 km was driven over a stretch the optimal route covers in 0.80 km, adding 2.13 km and straying up to 954 m from the optimal route (F3).
No rider consent exists for that segment: the chat record contains no in-app messages at all, so there is no rider message before 12:12 agreeing to any route or stop (F7).

The driver's claim that the GPS rerouted him (F8) is a post-trip statement contradicted by the system record of a 954 m excursion from the optimal route (F3), and RD-5 disregards after-the-fact explanations where no prior rider agreement is on record.

The driver cannot rely on the congestion exception: the only traffic facts are speed bands of 30–39 km/h and 40–49 km/h (F9, F10, i.e. bands 4 and 5, not the band 1–2 severe congestion of RD-4(b)), and there were no recorded incidents at all during the trip window (F11), with fair weather and no rain (F12).
The billed excess distance is quantified in the fare record as $3.26 (2.31 km × $1.4097/km, this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km) (F4), which is the amount attributable to the unexcused segment.
The driver's 90-day record shows 4 disputes with 2 upheld, both on route (F14); added to this upheld case it makes his route deviation conduct repeated, supporting an account flag.

weaknesses: The segment 2.13 km (F3) is slightly larger than the whole-trip excess 2.31 km, of which only $3.26 was billed (F4); the driver will argue the 954 m excursion was ordinary map-matching wobble along the Ayer Rajah Expressway corridor and that the whole-trip delta is the only reliable figure.

The driver's GPS-reroute story (F8) has some support in the traffic facts he cannot fully be blamed for avoiding: Ayer Rajah Expressway at band 4 and Jurong Town Hall Road at band 5 (F9, F10) were slow, and a judge might treat that as a plausible (though not RD-4-compliant) motive for a detour.

There is no in-app chat at all (F7), so I cannot show the rider ever asked for the shortest route either; the rider's own 90-day profile shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F13), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of complaints rather than a genuine overcharge.

claims.assertion: The ride was a RydeTAXI metered trip (F6 shows base + distance + time units totalling $24.80), so extra kilometres driven flow straight into the fare and any unexcused deviation is refundable per RD-2's metered branch.

The GPS record shows the trip covered 10.7 km against an optimal 8.4 km, i.e. +2.3 km (+27%) more than the shortest and most direct route (F1), which the driver was obliged to take absent reasonable cause.

The excess is concentrated in a single off-route segment 12:12–12:16, where 2.93 km was driven over a stretch the optimal route covers in 0.80 km, adding 2.13 km and straying up to 954 m from the optimal route (F3).
No rider consent exists for that segment: the chat record contains no in-app messages at all, so there is no rider message before 12:12 agreeing to any route or stop (F7).

The driver's claim that the GPS rerouted him (F8) is a post-trip statement contradicted by the system record of a 954 m excursion from the optimal route (F3), and RD-5 disregards after-the-fact explanations where no prior rider agreement is on record.

The driver cannot rely on the congestion exception: the only traffic facts are speed bands of 30–39 km/h and 40–49 km/h (F9, F10, i.e. bands 4 and 5, not the band 1–2 severe congestion of RD-4(b)), and there were no recorded incidents at all during the trip window (F11), with fair weather and no rain (F12).
The billed excess distance is quantified in the fare record as $3.26 (2.31 km × $1.4097/km, this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km) (F4), which is the amount attributable to the unexcused segment.
The driver's 90-day record shows 4 disputes with 2 upheld, both on route (F14); added to this upheld case it makes his route deviation conduct repeated, supporting an account flag.

weaknesses: The segment 2.13 km (F3) is slightly larger than the whole-trip excess 2.31 km, of which only $3.26 was billed (F4); the driver will argue the 954 m excursion was ordinary map-matching wobble along the Ayer Rajah Expressway corridor and that the whole-trip delta is the only reliable figure.

The driver's GPS-reroute story (F8) has some support in the traffic facts he cannot fully be blamed for avoiding: Ayer Rajah Expressway at band 4 and Jurong Town Hall Road at band 5 (F9, F10) were slow, and a judge might treat that as a plausible (though not RD-4-compliant) motive for a detour.

There is no in-app chat at all (F7), so I cannot show the rider ever asked for the shortest route either; the rider's own 90-day profile shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F13), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of complaints rather than a genuine overcharge.

claims.assertion: The trip is RydeTAXI and was charged on the meter ($24.80, distance 10.74 km), so any route-deviation remedy is limited to the metered mileage units of an unexempted segment — not to the whole $3.26 excess shown in the fare breakdown.
Only one off-route segment exists (12:12–12:16), adding 2.13 km; the remaining 0.18 km of the +2.31 km excess is map-matching/loop noise that RD-2 expressly leaves unrefunded.

The driver explained the deviation as a GPS reroute, which is the routing practice Ryde permits when choosing the fastest or most efficient route; the statement is recorded but is not by itself an exemption.

RD-4 exemption is not available on this record: the only traffic items are speed bands 4 (30–39 km/h) on Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road — neither is band 1 or 2 — and no traffic incident is recorded near the route during the trip window.
No rider consent exists for the segment: the chat record contains no in-app messages at all, so there is no rider message sent before the 12:12 segment start agreeing to any route.

Because the segment is unexempted, the refund on the metered excess is 2.13 km × $1.4097/km = $3.00 (2.13 × 1.4097 = 3.0034), computed from the unexempted segment's extra_km and this trip's per-km rate.

No flag_account should attach: the four profile fields show the rider's own 90-day record is clean (0 disputes upheld) and, which matters more, the two route disputes upheld against the driver in 90 days fall short of making this case 'repeated' only if the adjudicator reads RD-6's window strictly; the driver asks the adjudicator to note the driver's 963 trips in 90 days against 2 upheld route disputes.
